full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and order dated 6-9-1994 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 and the judgment and order dated 25-5-1996 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Review Miscellaneous case No. 358 of 1994 dismissing the same. 

 4. On a review of evidence the trial Court decreed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 13-10-1991 and being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendant No.1 petitioner preferred Title Appeal No. 417 of 1991 in the court of the District Judge, Dhaka which was transferred to the court of the 5th Additional District Judge, Dhaka for disposal on 15-5-1993. The learned 5th Additional District Judge, Dhaka dismissed the appeal for default vide order dated 15-5-1993 and against the said order the defendant No.1 petitioner filed an application under Order XLI rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure for re-admission of the appeal after setting aside the order of dismissal for default and the said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1993. The plaintiff opposite party contested the said Miscellaneous case and the learned 5th Additional District Judge after hearing the parties vide his judgment and order dated 26-1-1994 dismissed the aforesaid Miscellaneous case No. 5 of 1993. Thereafter, against the said order the present petitioner filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 under Order XLIII rule 1(t) of the Code of Civil Procedure in the court of the District Judge, Dhaka and the said appeal as usual was contested by the opposite party and ultimately the learned District Judge, after hearing both the parities dismissed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 vide his judgment and order dated 6-9-1994. Against the said order the present petitioner filed a Review Miscellaneous Case No. 358 of 1994 on 29-11-1994 under Order XLVII rule I read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before learned District Judge and the learned District Judge, after hearing both the parties also dismissed the said Review Miscellaneous Case No. 358 of 1994 by his judgment and order dated 25-5-1994 and ultimately the defendant appellant petitioner filed the present Revisional Application before this court impugning the order dated 6-9-1994 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 and the order dated 25-5-1996 passed in Review Miscellaneous. Case No. 358 of 1994 and Rule was issued and in the due course the plaintiff opposite parties entered appearance and filed court Affidavit. 

 6. At the time of hearing the Rule both the parties advanced their arguments at length on merits in support of their cases. After closing his argument Mr Rahman, who appeared for the opposite parties, sought for leave to allow Mr Md Nurul Amin to make some submissions on point of law and the prayer was, allowed. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing with the leave of the court, submitted that the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 and the Review Miscellaneous Case No. 358 of 1994 were incompetent and not maintainable in view of the provisions as laid down in Order XLIII rule 1(t) read with section 106 of the Code of Civil Procedure inasmuch as the Miscellaneous. Case No. 5 of 1993 was dismissed by the learned 5th Additional District Judge, Dhaka under Order XLI rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure and, as such, an appeal would lie before the High Court Division against that order instead of rule I Sub-rule (t) of Order XLIII of the Code. But unfortunately, this important question of law was missed by, the learned Advocate of both parties as well as the learned District Judge, in entertaining the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 and the subsequent Review Miscellaneous Case No. 358 of 1994. Not only that even before me this important question of law was not mooted by the engaged lawyers of the parties and it is. only Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate, who, appearing with leave of the court, pointed out correct position of law and, as such, aster hearing the learned Advocate of both the sides the matter was fixed today for delivery of judgment giving a chance to the learned Advocate Mr Abul Kalam Azad to see if he can find anything to refute the argument advanced by Mr Md Nurul Amin and Mr Md Abul Kalam Azad in due course appeared and failed to add anything to his former argument. 

 7. On a perusal of Order XLIII rule 1(t) read with section 106 of the Code of Civil Procedure, it is crystal clear that in the instant case the learned District Judge, Dhaka had no jurisdiction whatsoever to entertain the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 as well as the Review Miscellaneous Case No. 358 of 1994 and, as such, the orders dated 6-9-1994 and 25-5-1996 passed in the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 and Review Miscellaneous. Case No. 358 of 1994 respectively are nullities and they have no existence in the eye of the law. Since the Miscellaneous Appeal as well as the Miscellaneous. Review case are incompetent and not maintainable in law and the said order being nullity in the eye of law, I do not find any substance in this revision application and I do not, find any scope to enter into the merits of this Rule. 

 8. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The Miscellaneous Appeal No. 39 of 1994 is sent back to the learned District Judge for passing an order in accordance with law for presenting the same before the proper court.
